name: STM32H750VBT6
title: STM32H750xB Arm Cortex-M7 microcontrollers, up to 480 MHz, 128 Kbytes flash, 1 Mbyte RAM, crypto, LCD-TFT and JPEG, 1.62 V to 3.6 V
summary: A high-performance Cortex-M7 microcontroller line with a double-precision FPU and 16 + 16 Kbytes of L1 cache, clocked at up to 480 MHz on revision V silicon (400 MHz otherwise). It pairs a small 128 Kbyte flash with 1 Mbyte of RAM (192 Kbytes of TCM, 864 Kbytes of user SRAM, 4 Kbytes of backup SRAM), with a Quad-SPI port and an FMC for external memory. Peripherals include three 16-bit ADCs, two 12-bit DACs, comparators and op-amps, a 2.1 ns high-resolution timer, Ethernet, two USB OTG, two FDCAN, an LCD-TFT controller, a JPEG codec, DMA2D, AES/TDES/HASH and a true RNG, in LQFP100 to TFBGA240+25 packages.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M7 with double-precision FPU, up to 480 MHz (revision V) or 400 MHz
1 Mbyte: 64 KB ITCM + 128 KB DTCM, 864 KB user SRAM, 4 KB backup SRAM
1.62 V to 3.6 V (1.71 V min on LQFP100 or with the internal PDR on)
3 x 16-bit, up to 36 channels, up to 3.6 MSPS

tables.title: STM32H750xB features and peripheral counts
notes: (1) The LQFP144 package has no SDRAM interface.
(2) SPI1, SPI2 and SPI3 each run either as SPI or as I2S audio, one mode at a time.
(3) 480 MHz is reached only on revision V devices.
(4) At 480 MHz the junction temperature is limited to -40 to +105 °C.
(5) LQFP100 has no PDR_ON pin; it is tied to VDD inside, so VDD must be at least 1.71 V.
(6) VDD/VDDA may go down to 1.62 V only with an external supervisor and PDR_ON tied to VSS; with the internal power detector enabled the floor is 1.71 V.
(7) The junction temperature is limited to -40 to +125 °C.

circuits.description: Pin parameters are measured with a 50 pF capacitor from the MCU pin to ground.
notes: PA0 stands for any pin.

circuits.title: Pin input voltage
circuits.description: A pin's input voltage VIN is the level a source holds on the MCU pin, measured against ground.
notes: PA0 stands for any pin.

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: Ceramic decoupling on every supply pair, placed at the pins or under them on the back of the board. VDD takes one 100 nF per VDD pin plus one 4.7 µF; VDDLDO, the regulator's input, takes 4.7 µF; each of the two VCAP pins takes 2.2 µF for the core regulator. VDDA and VREF+ each take 100 nF plus 1 µF to VSSA, and VREF- returns to VSSA. VDD33USB takes 1 µF and 100 nF, VDD50USB, the USB regulator's input, 100 nF. A 1.2 V to 3.6 V source on VBAT keeps the backup domain (LSE, RTC, wakeup logic, backup registers and backup RAM) running through the internal power switch.

parts.note: at the first VCAP pin, ESR below 100 mΩ
at the second VCAP pin, ESR below 100 mΩ

notes: A tolerance of ±20 % on the decoupling capacitors is acceptable.
VREF+ may be tied to VDDA, and VDD33USB to VDD50USB; both links are optional.
VDDLDO, VDD50USB and VREF- are balls of the larger packages only; VDD33USB is absent on LQFP100.
With the regulator bypassed, the two 2.2 µF VCAP capacitors give way to two 100 nF decoupling capacitors.
Removing decoupling capacitors to save board area or cost can make the device misbehave.

circuits.title: Current consumption measurement
circuits.description: Supply current is measured as IDD into the joined VDD and VDDA supply, and as IDD_VBAT into VBAT, each through its own ammeter.

circuits.title: 8 MHz crystal on the HSE oscillator
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal or resonator across OSC_IN and OSC_OUT, a load capacitor CL1 from OSC_IN and CL2 from the crystal's other side to ground, and REXT in series between the crystal and OSC_OUT. The feedback resistor RF and the bias-controlled gain stage are inside the part. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces the crystal and both capacitors.

parts.note: high-frequency ceramic, matched to the crystal
high-frequency ceramic, usually equal to CL1

notes: Crystal and capacitors go as close to the oscillator pins as possible.

circuits.title: 32.768 kHz crystal on the LSE oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal or resonator across OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT with load capacitor CL1 from OSC32_IN and CL2 from OSC32_OUT to ground. RF and the gain stage are inside the part, and no resistor is fitted across the crystal. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces the crystal and both capacitors.
notes: Fitting a resistor between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT is not allowed.

circuits.title: NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground keeps parasitic resets out, and a push-button to ground resets the part by hand; the pull-up RPU and the reset filter are inside. The external reset circuit must pull NRST below VIL(NRST) max.

notes: PA0 stands for any ADC input pin.

operation.text: STM32H750VB comes in LQFP100, ZB in LQFP144, IB in LQFP176 or UFBGA176+25 and XB in TFBGA240+25; the part numbers differ in I/O count, wakeup and tamper pins and ADC channel count. All run from -40 to +85 °C ambient. Every package except LQFP100 has its own USB supply inputs.

Arm Cortex-M7 with a double-precision FPU (IEEE 754, single and double precision) and the DSP instruction set; it runs Cortex-M4 binaries. Six-stage dual-issue pipeline with dynamic branch prediction and Harvard L1 caches of 16 Kbytes for instructions and 16 Kbytes for data. Interfaces: a 64-bit AXI master, a 64-bit ITCM port, two 32-bit DTCM ports and a low-latency AHB-Lite peripheral port (AHBP). Up to 480 MHz, 1027 DMIPS (2.14 DMIPS/MHz).

Up to 16 regions, each divisible into 8 subregions, with programmable base, size (32 bytes to 4 Gbytes) and attributes, separate rules for privileged and user accesses. A violation raises a memory-management exception. It must be set up and enabled before it acts.
128 Kbytes of flash for program and data, from which the device can boot, plus 2 Kbytes (64 flash words) of user option bytes.

Beside the RDP and PCROP read protections, a Secure access mode runs secure services straight after reset, ahead of any other code; once they finish, their code and data can no longer be read. Two kinds exist: ST root secure services in system memory, for installing firmware and third-party modules with cryptography keyed to a private key unique to each device; and user secure services kept in user flash areas chosen by option bytes (for example a firmware updater or a flash integrity check). Only the Cortex-M7 in Secure access mode reaches those option bytes and secured areas; other bus masters cannot.

512 Kbytes of AXI SRAM in D1; SRAM1 (128 Kbytes), SRAM2 (128 Kbytes) and SRAM3 (32 Kbytes) in D2; SRAM4 (64 Kbytes) in D3; 4 Kbytes of backup SRAM, write-protected against stray accesses and kept in Standby and VBAT modes. TCM: 64 Kbytes of ITCM RAM on the 64-bit ITCM port for time-critical code, and 128 Kbytes of DTCM RAM as two 64 Kbyte banks on the two 32-bit DTCM ports, usable in parallel by the dual-issue core. Both TCMs run at zero wait states and are reachable by the CPU and by the MDMA (also in Sleep mode) through the CPU AHBS slave port; the MDMA can preload code or data into them.

SRAM is protected by single-error-correct, double-error-detect ECC: 7 check bits on each 32-bit word; AXI SRAM and ITCM RAM use 8 check bits on each 64-bit word. Bit errors from ageing or radiation are expected over the product life and are to be handled by application software.

The BOOT0 pin together with the BOOT_ADDx option bytes selects the boot address, anywhere from 0x0000 0000 to 0x3FFF FFFF: the whole flash, the ITCM, DTCM and SRAMs, or the system-memory bootloader. The bootloader reprograms the flash over USART, I2C, SPI or USB-DFU (application note AN2606).

VCORE feeds three domains that can be clock-gated or switched off separately: D1 (Cortex-M7 and high-performance peripherals), D2 (most peripherals, communication and timers) and D3 (reset, clock and power control plus some peripherals). The USB block has a 3.3 V regulator of its own for the internal PHYs, which lets VDD differ from 3.3 V.

While VDD is under 1 V, VDDA, VDD33USB and VDD50USB must stay below VDD + 300 mV; once VDD is above 1 V the supplies are independent. During power-down VDD may briefly sit below the other supplies only while the energy delivered to the chip stays under 1 mJ, so decoupling capacitors may discharge with different time constants.

A power-on reset holds the device in reset while VDD is under a fixed threshold; a power-down reset asserts reset when VDD falls below a fixed threshold and is switched on or off with the PDR_ON pin; a brownout reset offers three thresholds between 2.1 V and 2.7 V chosen by option bytes. A programmable voltage detector (PVD) is also present.

With the internal power-down detector active, VDD must stay above 1.71 V. Operation down to 1.62 V needs an external supervisor with PDR_ON tied to VSS. LQFP100 has no PDR_ON pin (tied to VDD inside), so its minimum VDD is 1.71 V. With PDR_ON at VSS the VBAT function is lost and VBAT is tied to VDD.

One LDO supplies D1, D2 and D3; D1 and D2 can be powered down on their own. Six output levels: in Run, VOS0 (boosted, LDO only), VOS1 (high performance), VOS2 (medium) and VOS3 (lowest power); in Stop, SVOS3 keeps the Stop-wakeup peripherals (UART, SPI, I2C, LPTIM) running, while SVOS4 and SVOS5 turn them off and the device still wakes on a GPIO or asynchronous interrupt. A separate backup regulator gives about 0.9 V.

Six modes, from lightest to deepest: CSleep halts the CPU clock; CStop halts the clocks of the CPU subsystem; DStop halts the bus-matrix clock of one domain; Stop halts the system clock; DStandby removes power from one domain; Standby removes power from the system. WFI or WFE, or leaving an interrupt handler with SLEEPONEXIT set, puts the CPU into CSleep or CStop. A domain goes to DStop or DStandby once the CPU, its subsystem and that domain's peripherals are all in a low-power state; the whole system enters Stop or Standby when no EXTI wakeup source is pending and the domains are in DStop or DStandby. Standby draws 2.95 µA with backup SRAM off and RTC/LSE on. Pins can report CPU and domain power state.

The RCC sits in D3 and generates, gates and resets all clocks. Internal oscillators: HSI 64 MHz, HSI48 48 MHz, CSI 4 MHz and LSI 32 kHz. External: HSE from 4 to 50 MHz as an external clock or 4 to 48 MHz with a crystal or ceramic resonator, and LSE at 32.768 kHz. Three PLLs with fractional mode, one for the system clock and two for kernel clocks. The device starts on HSI. Peripherals with a separate kernel clock keep their baud rate when the system clock changes.

Power-on reset clears every register. A system reset clears everything except debug, part of the RCC, the power controller status registers and the backup domain. A system reset comes from: power-on reset, brownout, a low level on NRST, either watchdog (window or independent), a software request, a security reset on low-power entry, or leaving Standby.

Up to 168 I/Os, all able to raise interrupts, all high-current-capable with selectable speed. Software sets each one as an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), an output (push-pull or open-drain, optionally with pull-up or pull-down), or a peripheral alternate function. Out of reset every GPIO except the debug pins sits in analog mode. A locking sequence freezes the I/O configuration.

A 64-bit AXI bus matrix in D1, a 32-bit AHB bus matrix in D2 and another in D3, joined by AHB links between domains, with five AHB-to-APB and two AXI-to-AHB bridges. D1 masters: CPU AXI port, SDMMC1, MDMA, DMA2D, LTDC; D1 slaves: flash, AXI SRAM, QSPI, FMC, AHB3/APB3. D2 masters: DMA1, DMA2, Ethernet MAC, SDMMC2, USBHS1, USBHS2 and the CPU AHBP port; D2 slaves: SRAM1-3, AHB1, AHB2, APB1, APB2. D3: BDMA master, AHB4/APB4, SRAM4 and backup SRAM.

Four controllers. MDMA in D1: 16 channels, single-block, repeated-block and linked-list transfers between any memories and peripherals, with an AXI master and an AHB path to the TCMs; it can work with the D2 DMAs or serve peripheral requests itself. DMA1 and DMA2 in D2: dual-port, 8 streams each, with FIFOs. BDMA in D3. A request router (DMAMUX) maps peripheral requests to the controllers and can raise requests from peripheral triggers or DMA events.

Graphics DMA for filling a rectangle with one colour, copying a rectangle, copying with colour-format conversion, and blending two layers with conversion. Formats from 4 bpp indirect to 32 bpp direct colour, with on-chip colour lookup tables and block-based YCbCr input for JPEG decoder output. Interrupts at completion or at a programmed watermark; runs without the CPU or the other DMAs.
16 priority levels, up to 150 maskable interrupt channels plus the 16 Cortex-M7 interrupt lines; low latency with tail chaining, late-arrival handling and automatic context save and restore.
89 event/interrupt lines: 28 configurable (own pending flag, edge selection, software trigger) and 61 direct (from peripheral status flags). It can wake the CPU, the power domains or D3 from Stop.
CRC unit with a programmable polynomial, for checking data transfer or storage integrity, including flash checks in the scope of EN/IEC 60335-1.

Flexible memory controller for SRAM, PSRAM (4 banks), NOR/OneNAND flash, NAND flash with hardware ECC over up to 8 Kbytes, and SDRAM/mobile LPSDR SDRAM, on an 8-, 16- or 32-bit bus. Each bank has its own chip select and configuration; write FIFO, plus a read FIFO for SDRAM. The synchronous clock (FMC_CLK/FMC_SDCLK) is at most the FMC kernel clock divided by 2; synchronous SRAM, PSRAM and NOR run up to 133 MHz. No SDRAM on LQFP144.

Interface for single, dual or quad SPI flash, single or double data rate, dual-memory mode, up to 133 MHz. Modes: indirect through registers, automatic status polling, and memory-mapped with code execution and 8-, 16- or 32-bit reads. Up to 256 Mbytes of external flash can be mapped; opcode and frame format are programmable.

Three ADCs with 16, 14, 12, 10 or 8-bit resolution, up to 3.6 MSPS, up to 36 channels in all; each ADC shares up to 20 external channels. Single-shot or scan conversion, simultaneous and interleaved sample-and-hold, DMA, and an analog watchdog on one, several or all channels raising an interrupt outside programmed thresholds. Triggers from TIM1, TIM2, TIM3, TIM4, TIM6, TIM8, TIM15, HRTIM1 and LPTIM1.

Gives a voltage VTS linear with junction temperature from -40 to +125 °C, connected inside to ADC3_IN18; conversion range 1.7 V to 3.6 V. Its offset varies from part to part, so uncalibrated it suits only change detection; each device carries factory calibration data in read-only system memory.

The backup domain (RTC, backup registers, backup SRAM) runs from VDD while present and switches to the VBAT pin when the PDR sees VDD fall below its level. VBAT may come from a battery, a supercapacitor, or VDD itself (then VBAT mode does nothing). In VBAT operation, external interrupts and RTC alarms or events do not bring the device out of it. VBAT mode supports battery charging.

Two buffered 12-bit DAC channels, 1 MHz, each with its own converter. Monotonic in 8-bit and 12-bit modes; 12-bit data may be left- or right-aligned. Synchronized update, noise and triangle wave generation, independent or simultaneous dual conversion, DMA per channel with underrun detection, and external triggers including timer update outputs. Reference: VREF+ or the internal VREFBUF.

Two rail-to-rail ultra-low-power comparators, COMP1 and COMP2, with programmable reference, hysteresis, speed (slow for low power) and output polarity. Reference: an I/O, a DAC channel, or the internal reference or 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 of it. They wake the device from Stop, raise interrupts and timer breaks, and pair into a window comparator.

Two rail-to-rail op-amps, OPAMP1 and OPAMP2, with both inputs and the output on pins. Follower or PGA: non-inverting gain 2, 4, 8 or 16, inverting gain -1, -3, -7 or -15. Positive input can come from the DAC; output goes to an internal ADC. Input bias as low as 1 nA, input offset as low as 1.5 mV, GBW reaching 7.3 MHz.

One digital filter for sigma-delta modulators with 4 filter modules and 8 serial input channels, or 8 internal parallel inputs (ADC data or memory streams over DMA, up to 16 bits). Serial inputs: SPI or Manchester (1-wire) format, PDM microphones with PDM-to-PCM conversion; input clock up to 20 MHz (10 MHz Manchester); clock output 0 to 20 MHz for modulators. Filters: Sinc order 1 to 5 with oversampling up to 1024, plus integrator with oversampling 1 to 256; up to 24-bit signed output, offset correction, continuous or single conversion, regular and injected conversions. Triggers: software, timers, external events, or synchronously with filter 0. Analog watchdog with its own Sinc filter (order 1 to 3, oversampling 1 to 32), short-circuit detector counting 1 to 256 equal bits, break outputs, extremes detector, DMA and interrupts.

Parallel 8-, 10-, 12- or 14-bit input from camera modules and CMOS sensors, up to 140 Mbyte/s with an 80 MHz PIXCLK. Programmable polarity of PIXCLK, HSYNC and VSYNC; monochrome or raw Bayer, YCbCr 4:2:2, RGB 565 or compressed (JPEG) data; continuous or single-frame capture; hardware cropping.

24-bit parallel RGB output for LCD and TFT panels up to XGA (1024 x 768). Two layers, each with a 64 x 64-bit FIFO and a 256-entry x 24-bit colour lookup table, up to 8 input colour formats per layer, alpha blending (constant or from the data), colour keying, up to 4 interrupt events, and an AXI master with 16-word bursts.

Hardware JPEG encoder and decoder (ISO/IEC 10918-1) with header generation and parsing: 8 bits per channel, one sample per clock for encoding and decoding, up to four quantization tables, programmable Huffman tables (two AC, two DC) and minimum coded unit, single greyscale component, encode or decode (not both at once), and a high-speed decode setting.
True random number generator delivering 32-bit samples from an analog entropy source with internal conditioning.
DES/TDES in ECB and CBC with 64-, 128- or 192-bit keys; AES in ECB, CBC, GCM, CCM and CTR with 128-, 192- or 256-bit keys; hashing with SHA-1, SHA-2, MD5 and HMAC; DMA requests.

Counts: HRTIM1 (1), TIM1 and TIM8 advanced-control (2), ten general-purpose, TIM6 and TIM7 basic (2), LPTIM1 to LPTIM5 (5), plus the independent and window watchdogs and SysTick. Every timer counter can be frozen in debug.

Six timers (one master, five slaves) with 10 high-resolution outputs, pairable with dead-time insertion, 5 fault inputs and 10 external event inputs (current limit, zero-voltage or zero-current switching). The digital kernel is clocked at 480 MHz; high resolution (2.1 ns) is available on all ten outputs whether duty cycle, frequency or on-time is the quantity varied. Blanking and filtering of events and faults, DMA requests, a burst-mode controller, push-pull and resonant modes. Supported topologies include LLC, phase-shifted full bridge, buck or boost in voltage or current mode, lighting, or a high-resolution PWM DAC.

16-bit timers acting as three-phase PWM generators over 6 channels, with complementary outputs and programmable dead time, or as full general-purpose timers. Four channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM (0 to 100 %) and one-pulse output. Linked with other timers for synchronization or event chaining; DMA requests of their own.

TIM2 and TIM5 (32-bit) and TIM3 and TIM4 (16-bit) count up, down or up/down with a 16-bit prescaler and 4 channels each (up to 16 capture/compare/PWM channels), DMA, quadrature encoder input and inputs for 1 to 4 Hall sensors. TIM12 and TIM15 (2 channels) and TIM13, TIM14, TIM16, TIM17 (1 channel) are 16-bit up-counters with a 16-bit prescaler, synchronizable with TIM2-TIM5 or usable as time bases.
16-bit time bases mainly used to trigger the DAC and its waveform generation, each with its own DMA request.

LPTIM1 to LPTIM5: 16-bit up-counter with 16-bit autoreload and compare, pulse or PWM output, continuous or one-shot, software or hardware trigger, glitch filter and encoder mode. Clock from LSE, LSI, HSI, APB or an external input (counting even with no internal clock running). Clocked from LSE, LSI or the external input they keep running in Stop and can wake the device.

12-bit down-counter with 8-bit prescaler clocked by the 32 kHz LSI, so it keeps running in Stop and Standby; resets the device or serves as a free-running timeout timer. Started by hardware or software, chosen by option byte.
7-bit down-counter clocked from the main clock, with an early-warning interrupt; can be frozen in debug.
24-bit down-counter with autoreload, an interrupt at zero and a programmable clock source, meant for an RTOS tick.

BCD calendar with sub-seconds, seconds, minutes, hours (12/24 h), weekday, date, month and year, with automatic month-length and leap-year correction. Two alarms, shift correction from 1 to 32767 RTC clock pulses, 50 or 60 Hz reference clock input, digital calibration with 0.95 ppm resolution, three tamper pins with filtering, timestamp on a pin event, a tamper event or the switch to VBAT, and a 17-bit wakeup timer. 32 backup registers (128 bytes) survive system and power resets and Standby wakeup, holding data while VDD is absent. Clock: LSE crystal or external clock, LSI (about 32 kHz) or HSE/32. With LSE the RTC works in VBAT and every low-power mode; with LSI it works in low-power modes but not in VBAT. Alarm, wakeup, timestamp and tamper events can wake the device.

Four I2C interfaces, I2C-bus rev. 5 compatible: master and slave, multimaster, Standard-mode to 100 kbit/s, Fast-mode to 400 kbit/s and Fast-mode Plus to 1 Mbit/s with 20 mA drive, 7- and 10-bit and multiple 7-bit addresses, programmable setup and hold, optional clock stretching. SMBus 2.0 (hardware PEC, ARP, alert) and PMBus 1.1. Independent kernel clock, wakeup from Stop on address match, programmable analog and digital filters, DMA on a 1-byte buffer.

USART1, USART2, USART3, USART6 and UART4, UART5, UART7, UART8, up to 12.5 Mbit/s: asynchronous, IrDA SIR, multiprocessor, single-wire half-duplex, LIN master/slave, CTS/RTS flow control and RS485 driver enable. The four USARTs add smartcard (ISO 7816) and SPI-like synchronous modes. 16-entry transmit and receive FIFOs, off by default. A kernel clock independent of the CPU lets each wake the device from Stop on a start bit, any frame, a chosen frame or a FIFO level. All served by DMA.

One low-power UART (LPUART1) with half-duplex single-wire, CTS/RTS and multiprocessor modes, FIFOs, DMA and wakeup from Stop like the USARTs. From the 32.768 kHz LSE alone it runs up to 9600 baud, so it can wait for a frame in Stop at very low power; faster clocks give higher rates.

Six SPIs (SPI2S1, SPI2S2, SPI2S3, SPI4, SPI5, SPI6) up to 150 Mbit/s, master or slave, full-duplex, half-duplex or simplex; 3-bit prescaler (8 master frequencies), 4- to 16-bit frames, NSS pulse mode, TI mode, hardware CRC, 8 x 8-bit Rx and Tx FIFOs with DMA. Three I2S interfaces share SPI1, SPI2 and SPI3: master or slave, simplex or full-duplex, 16- or 32-bit, 8 kHz to 192 kHz, master clock output at 256 x Fs, 16 x 8-bit FIFOs with DMA; their clock can come from a dedicated audio PLL or an external clock. One more I2S sits in the low-power domain.

Four serial audio interfaces (SAI1 to SAI4) for I2S, LSB- or MSB-justified, PCM/DSP, TDM and AC'97, with SPDIF output when transmitting. Each has two audio sub-blocks with their own clock generator and I/O control, receiver or transmitter, synchronous or not, and SAIs can be synchronized with each other. Up to 192 kHz; a PDM interface handles up to 6 microphones.

S/PDIF receiver for IEC-60958 and IEC-61937 streams (stereo up to high sample rates, compressed surround up to 5.1): up to 4 inputs, automatic symbol-rate detection, symbol rate up to 12.288 MHz, stereo from 32 to 192 kHz, parity handling, DMA for audio and for control/user channel data, interrupts. It outputs spdif_frame_sync, toggling at the sub-frame rate, for clock-drift tracking.

Single-wire protocol master for a contactless front end per ETSI TS 102 613: full-duplex, automatic bus state handling (active, suspend, resume), bit rate programmable to 2 Mbit/s, start-of-frame, end-of-frame and CRC handled in hardware, DMA.

MDIO slave with 32 register addresses, each with a 16-bit output data register (firmware read/write, MDIO read) and a 16-bit input data register (firmware read, MDIO write), configurable port address, maskable interrupts on register write, register read and protocol error; works in and wakes from Stop.
Two SD/SDIO/MMC hosts up to 125 MHz: MMC 4.51 with 1-, 4- or 8-bit bus, SD memory 4.1 and SDIO 4.0 with 1- or 4-bit bus, one card at a time each, with a built-in DMA.

Two CAN modules, ISO 11898-1 (CAN 2.0 A, B) and CAN FD 1.0. FDCAN1 also supports time-triggered CAN (ISO 11898-4) with global time and drift compensation. A shared 10 Kbyte message RAM holds filters, receive FIFOs and buffers, transmit event FIFOs and transmit buffers. An optional clock calibration unit derives a calibrated CAN clock from HSI and the PLL by watching frames received on FDCAN1.

Two USB 2.0 OTG controllers: OTG_HS1 does full and high speed (480 Mbit/s, high speed needs an external ULPI PHY on 12 signals, SDR, with a 60 MHz clock), OTG_HS2 full speed only. Both have an internal full-speed PHY (12 Mbit/s) and can run from HSI48 without a crystal. 4 Kbytes of shared dynamic FIFO, SRP and HNP, 9 bidirectional endpoints, 16 host channels with periodic OUT, OTG 1.3/2.0, LPM, Battery Charging 1.2, internal DMA, no external resistors needed. A dedicated 48 MHz clock is needed. In host or OTG mode, a power switch is needed for bus-powered devices.

IEEE 802.3-2002 MAC for 10 and 100 Mbit/s with its own DMA, to an external PHY over MII (17 signals) or RMII (9 signals); the device can output the 25 MHz MII clock. VLAN tags, half-duplex (CSMA/CD) and full-duplex, control frames, 32-bit CRC insertion and removal, address filtering, 32-bit status per frame, 2 Kbyte transmit and receive FIFOs, IEEE 1588-2008 (PTP v2) timestamping with a comparator wired to a TIM2 input, and an interrupt when system time passes a target.
Hardware Consumer Electronics Control (HDMI supplement 1) controller with a kernel clock independent of the CPU; it can wake the device from Stop on received data.

SWD and JTAG debug ports, breakpoints, code and data trace (ETM, TRACECLK and TRACED[3:0]), serial-wire trace, trigger input and output, Arm CoreSight components and a 4 Kbyte embedded trace buffer. Each device has a 96-bit unique ID.

PC2_C, PC3_C, PA0_C and PA1_C are analog-only pads (TT_a). On TFBGA240+25 they are separate balls from PC2, PC3, PA0 and PA1, with the analog switch between them open. On the other packages PC2 and PC3 have only the _C pin, joined to the GPIO through the switch; closed, it brings the Pxy alternate functions to that pin. PA0_C and PA1_C exist only on TFBGA240+25. A SYSCFG register controls the switch.

PA13 is JTMS/SWDIO, PA14 JTCK/SWCLK, PA15 JTDI, PB3 JTDO/TRACESWO and PB4 NJTRST after reset; unlike the other GPIOs they do not start in analog mode. PH0 and PH1 come up as GPIO; PC14 and PC15 come up as OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT.
E1 is NC and must stay floating; K16, K17, L16, L17, M16, M17 and N17 are NC. F1 is reserved and must be tied to VSS or VDD, never left floating. F2 and G2 are tied to VSS.

operation.topic: Rev Y figures: how minimum, maximum and typical are meant
operation.text: Every voltage is taken from VSS. A minimum or maximum without a footnote is the worst case over junction temperature, supply and frequency, tested on every device in production at TJ = 25 °C and at the top of the chosen temperature range. Limits marked as coming from characterization, simulation or design are the mean plus or minus three standard deviations of a sample. A typical value is at TJ = 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V (within 1.7 V to 3.6 V), a design guide only and not tested; a typical ADC accuracy figure is one that 95 % of a characterized batch meets or beats over the whole temperature range (mean plus or minus two standard deviations). Typical curves are design guides, not tested.
Pin parameters are measured with 50 pF from the pin to ground; an input voltage is the level applied at the pin, taken from ground.

The main regulator is kept stable by an external capacitor CEXT on VCAP; two can be fitted, one on each VCAP pin. CEXT is modelled as a capacitance C with an equivalent series resistance ESR in series and a leakage resistance across it.

Supply current depends on supply voltage, ambient temperature, pin loading, software setup, clock frequencies, pin switching rate, where the program sits in memory and the code itself. It is measured with an ammeter in the VDD/VDDA feed and another in VBAT. Run-mode figures are taken running CoreMark, with every I/O in analog input mode, every peripheral off unless the row says otherwise, flash wait states at the minimum for the clock frequency, and, when peripherals are on, AHB at half the CPU clock and APB at half the AHB clock. Ambient temperature and supply are within the general operating conditions.

I/O current has a static and a dynamic share. Static: an input with its pull-up or pull-down draws current when the pin is held low from outside, worked out from the pull resistor values in the I/O static table; an output also feeds whatever pull resistors and load hang on it. An input sitting at an in-between voltage draws extra current through its Schmitt trigger, which putting the pin in analog mode avoids (ADC inputs belong in analog mode). A floating input can drift to such a level, or toggle, from outside noise; set unused pins to analog, or pull them, or make them outputs. Dynamic: a switching pin draws current to charge and discharge its load, internal plus external capacitance, measured with the pin as a push-pull output toggled in software at a fixed rate.

Each peripheral's figure is the difference between the current with every peripheral clock off and with only that peripheral clocked, at 25 °C ambient and VDD = 3.3 V, all I/Os starting in analog input mode, the I/O compensation cell on, fPCLK at a quarter and fHCLK at half the CPU clock frcc_c_ck, which is 400 MHz in VOS1 (Scale 1), 300 MHz in VOS2 and 200 MHz in VOS3.

Wakeup time runs from the wakeup event to the first instruction the CPU fetches. Stop and Sleep are left on a WFE event; the WKUP pin PC1 wakes the part from Standby, Stop and Sleep. Measured at ambient temperature with VDD = 3.3 V.

In bypass mode the HSE or LSE oscillator is off and OSC_IN (or OSC32_IN) acts as an ordinary I/O driven by an outside clock source, so the input levels of the I/O static table apply. The waveform is defined by its high and low levels (VHSEH/VHSEL, VLSEH/VLSEL) with 10 % and 90 % points for rise and fall times tr and tf, its high and low times tW and its period T.

The HSE oscillator runs from a 4 MHz to 48 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator; its figures come from characterization with typical external parts. Resonator and load capacitors sit as close to the oscillator pins as possible, which keeps distortion and start-up time down. CL1 and CL2 are high-quality ceramic capacitors made for high-frequency use and matched to the crystal, normally of equal value; the crystal's specified load capacitance is CL1 and CL2 in series, plus the pin and board capacitance, for which about 10 pF is a fair first estimate. The 200 kΩ feedback resistor RF is inside the part; an external REXT between the crystal and OSC_OUT is sized for the crystal. ST application note AN2867 covers crystal selection.

The LSE oscillator runs from a 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator, with load capacitors from each pin to ground, both as close to the pins as possible. Drive strength is set by LSEDRV[1:0] from low to high; each step up draws more current and allows a higher maximum critical crystal gm. Start-up, from the software enable to steady oscillation, is about 2 s with a standard crystal and varies widely with the crystal maker. ST application note AN2867 covers crystal selection.

Flash figures hold for TJ = –40 °C to 125 °C unless a row says otherwise. Parts leave the factory with the flash erased. A flash word of 266 bits is programmed at once; program and erase run with a parallelism of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits, the wider settings faster and drawing more current, and the 32-bit and 64-bit settings need at least 1.8 V.

Susceptibility is tested on samples during characterization, with the part running a simple program that toggles two LEDs through I/O ports and the LEDs showing a failure. Quad-SPI timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, edges measured at 0.5 VDD, the I/O compensation cell on, and HSLV on whenever VDD ≤ 2.7 V. Negative current injected into any analog input lowers the accuracy of a conversion running on another analog input badly, so it is to be avoided; a Schottky diode from pin to ground is recommended on analog pins that may inject negative current. Positive injection within the IINJ(PIN) and ΣIINJ(PIN) limits does not affect accuracy. The error terms are defined against the transfer curve, where 1 LSB = VREF+ / 2^n (or VDDA / 2^n) for resolution n: ET, total unadjusted error, is the largest deviation of the actual curve from the ideal; EO, offset error, the deviation of the first actual transition from the first ideal one; EG, gain error, the deviation of the last actual transition from the last ideal one; ED, differential linearity error, the largest deviation of an actual step from the ideal step; EL, integral linearity error, the largest deviation of any actual transition from the line joining the end points.

DFSDM timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, fPCLKx and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 30 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD; they apply to the DFSDMx_CKINx, DFSDMx_DATINx and DFSDMx_CKOUT pins. DCMI timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with DCMI_PIXCLK sampling on the falling edge, DCMI_VSYNC and DCMI_HSYNC active high, 14-bit data, a 30 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD.

LTDC timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with LCD_CLK polarity high, LCD_DE active low, LCD_VSYNC and LCD_HSYNC active high, a 24-bit colour format, output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 30 pF load, edges measured at 0.5 VDD and the I/O compensation cell on. SAI timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, fPCLKx and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 30 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD; they apply to SCK, SD and WS. The APB clock runs at least twice the SAI clock.

The levels and drive of FDCANx_TX and FDCANx_RX are those of the I/O port characteristics.

The USB interface complies fully with USB 2.0 and carries USB-IF certification as a full-speed device. operation.topic: USB OTG_HS ULPI timing conditions (rev Y)
operation.text: ULPI timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 20 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD. Control in is ULPI_DIR and ULPI_NXT, control out ULPI_STP, and data is 8 bits wide each way.

Ethernet SMI, RMII and MII timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature and frcc_c_ck, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 20 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD. SMI data on ETH_MDIO is timed against ETH_MDC, RMII signals against RMII_REF_CLK, and MII receive and transmit signals against MII_RX_CLK and MII_TX_CLK.

JTAG and SWD timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 0x10, a 30 pF load and edges measured at 0.5 VDD. TMS and TDI are sampled on TCK and TDO launched from it; SWDIO is sampled on and driven from SWCLK.

operation.topic: Rev V figures: how minimum, maximum and typical are meant
operation.text: Every voltage is taken from VSS. Limits marked as coming from characterization, simulation or design are the mean plus or minus three standard deviations of a sample. A typical value is at TJ = 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V (within 1.7 V to 3.6 V), a design guide only and not tested; a typical ADC accuracy figure is one that 95 % of a characterized batch meets or beats over the whole temperature range (mean plus or minus two standard deviations). Typical curves are design guides, not tested. These figures apply to silicon revision V.
Pin parameters are measured with 50 pF from the pin to ground; an input voltage is the level applied at the pin, taken from ground.

The main regulator is kept stable by an external capacitor CEXT on VCAP; two can be fitted, one on each VCAP pin. CEXT is modelled as a capacitance C with an equivalent series resistance ESR in series and a leakage resistance across it.

Supply current depends on supply voltage, ambient temperature, pin loading, software setup, clock frequencies, pin switching rate, where the program sits in memory and the code itself. It is measured with an ammeter in the VDD/VDDA feed and another in VBAT. Run-mode figures are taken running CoreMark, with every I/O in analog input mode, every peripheral off unless stated otherwise, flash wait states at the minimum for the clock frequency, and, when peripherals are on, AHB at half the CPU clock and APB at half the AHB clock. I/O current has a static and a dynamic share. An input sitting at an in-between voltage draws extra current through its Schmitt trigger, which putting the pin in analog mode avoids (ADC inputs belong in analog mode). A floating input can drift to such a level, or toggle, from outside noise; set unused pins to analog, or pull them, or make them outputs. Dynamic: a switching pin draws current to charge and discharge its load, internal plus external capacitance, measured with the pin as a push-pull output toggled in software at a fixed rate.

SDMMC timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, fPCLKx and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 0x11, a 30 pF load (20 pF above 100 MHz and in eMMC mode), edges measured at 0.5 VDD, the I/O compensation cell on, HSLV on whenever VDD ≤ 2.7 V and the core at VOS1. CMD and D are timed against CK. SD at 1.8 V needs an external voltage converter.

The USB interface complies fully with USB 2.0 and carries USB-IF certification as a full-speed device. USB works down to VDD33USB = 2.7 V, but between 2.7 V and 3.0 V the full electrical characteristics are not met. USB_DP (D+) and USB_DM (D-) need no external series termination resistors: the matching impedance is built into the driver.

operation.topic: USB OTG_HS ULPI timing conditions (rev V)
operation.text: ULPI timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, fPCLKx and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11, a 20 pF load, edges measured at 0.5 VDD, the I/O compensation cell on and the core at VOS1. Control in is ULPI_DIR and ULPI_NXT, control out ULPI_STP, and data is 8 bits wide each way.

Ethernet SMI, RMII and MII timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, a 20 pF load, edges measured at 0.5 VDD, the I/O compensation cell on, HSLV on whenever VDD ≤ 2.7 V and the core at VOS1. SMI data on ETH_MDIO is timed against ETH_MDC, RMII signals against RMII_REF_CLK, and MII receive and transmit signals against MII_RX_CLK and MII_TX_CLK.

JTAG and SWD timings hold over the general operating conditions for ambient temperature, frcc_c_ck and VDD, with output speed OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 0x10, a 30 pF load, edges measured at 0.5 VDD and the core at VOS1. TMS and TDI are sampled on TCK and TDO launched from it; SWDIO is sampled on and driven from SWCLK.
Parts marked ES or E, or delivered with an engineering-sample letter, are not qualified and are not for production use.
